outOfScope: Changing product WHAT or acceptance semantics to make an efficiency candidate pass.
Replacing Application domain authority, Oracle source ownership, Jev/QA judgment authority or EffectOperation truth.
Adopting Unreal Agent wholesale or treating its benchmark as ExHarness acceptance evidence.
constraints: Baseline and candidate use the exact same BB-077 model/provider identity, task inputs, tool surface, budgets, source fixture semantics and independent acceptance logic.
The held-out cohort is frozen to HOLD-F01, HOLD-F02, HOLD-C01 and HOLD-C02 from BB-077. No DEV-* task, replacement task or post-result task mutation may enter the acceptance cohort.
All task executions, retries, failures, timeouts, rate limits, unknown usage and human interventions remain visible. No best-of-k, success-only filtering or outlier deletion is permitted.
Accepted quality cannot be traded for savings. The exact BB-077 quality/safety and efficiency gates are reused without post-hoc tuning.
Unknown/missing cost or token accounting, a missing matched arm, or incomplete held-out execution yields INCONCLUSIVE; it is never coerced to zero or to PROMOTE_ASYNC.
PROMOTE_ASYNC changes only the supported Core HOW profile. EffectOperation truth, product acceptance, Application authority and Jev/QA judgment authority remain unchanged.

CORE_SYNC remains implemented, exported and regression-tested regardless of the decision. Rollback is a supported profile selection at a new/quiescent session boundary, not a live mid-effect state rewrite.
Worker execution requires BB-077, BB-078, BB-079 and BB-080 DONE and must bind their exact delivered artifacts/Living refs. Any incompatible delivered contract is PLAN_INPUT_CONTRADICTION.
Research/public reference benchmarks are motivation only. Only matched ExHarness held-out evidence may choose the supported profile.
invariants: Async scheduling and prompt optimization cannot become correctness, product-acceptance or external-effect authority.
Every detached operation remains bound to exact call/turn/action/effect identity and unresolved effect ambiguity fails closed.
Efficiency claims require matched evidence with fixed model, task semantics, tool surface and resource budget.
architectureDecisions: D0 — 2026-09-27 benchmark-program reset revokes the previous READY acceptance protocol. BB-081 returns to RESEARCH_SA so held-out async acceptance is derived from the unified harness-benchmark methodology rather than the old fixed four-task protocol.

D1 — BB-081 is acceptance/publication only. It must not change benchmark task semantics, provider/model identity, BB-077 primary thresholds, effect semantics, async scheduler correctness or the delivered BB-078–080 behavior to make the candidate pass.

D2 — The acceptance cohort is exactly four pre-registered paired task units: HOLD-F01, HOLD-F02, HOLD-C01 and HOLD-C02. These fixture seeds and expected-output digests were reserved by BB-077 before async candidate work. No extra task may be added after observing candidate results; a new task set requires a new cohort/version.

D3 — Each paired unit runs both `CORE_SYNC` control and exact delivered `CORE_ASYNC_FIRST_V1` candidate with the BB-077 provider contract: OpenRouter, `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.6`, Anthropic provider only, fallbacks disabled, same budgets and the frozen 2026-09-25 normalized price table. The async arm is additionally bound to exact DONE BB-078/079/080 artifact hashes.

D4 — Use deterministic counterbalanced arm order to reduce time/order bias without changing the pair: HOLD-F01 SYNC→ASYNC, HOLD-F02 ASYNC→SYNC, HOLD-C01 SYNC→ASYNC, HOLD-C02 ASYNC→SYNC. Every arm gets a fresh workspace/runtime/executor/event state and unique provider session_id; no provider session or fixture state crosses arms.

D5 — Sample size is the complete four-task paired holdout cohort. The existing BB-077 `maxAttemptsPerTask=2` remains a failure/retry ceiling, not best-of-k: retries are new recorded attempts, their usage/cost remains in the task total, and no completed failed task is replaced. The cohort is a product gate, not a statistical-significance study; paired ratios and optional bootstrap intervals are descriptive only.

D6 — Trusted benchmark code independently computes exact expected task results and required call/effect conditions. Model `return_result`, harness exit status and worker-authored summaries are candidate evidence only; they cannot mark a task ACCEPTED.

D7 — Reuse BB-077 failure accounting unchanged. Every provider request and capability attempt carries task/arm/attempt identity; provider failures, rate limits, retries and unknown fields remain in raw records. Any human intervention beyond starting/restarting the exact frozen runner is recorded and makes the affected pair INCONCLUSIVE unless the protocol explicitly permits it.

D8 — The quality gate is exactly BB-077: candidate accepted-task rate must be no lower than synchronous control on the complete registered cohort. A missing pair or incomplete acceptance record is INCONCLUSIVE, not a pass.

D9 — The safety/recovery gate is absolute: candidate duplicate external effects must be zero and all delivered BB-078/080 recovery/cancellation negatives must pass under the held-out profile. Lost terminal result, unsafe cancellation, stale-model dispatch or unresolved non-reconcilable effect blocks promotion and yields KEEP_SYNC_BASELINE when observed conclusively.

D10 — The efficiency gates are exactly BB-077 and all are conjunctive: median paired normalized provider cost ratio <=0.85, prompt-input-token ratio <=0.90, model-turn ratio <=1.00 and elapsed-time ratio <=1.10. Provider cached/cache-write tokens, useful operations/turn, overlap and latency remain explanatory; none may substitute for a failed primary gate.

D11 — The gate reducer returns exactly `PROMOTE_ASYNC`, `KEEP_SYNC_BASELINE` or `INCONCLUSIVE`. PROMOTE_ASYNC requires complete matched evidence plus every quality/safety/efficiency gate. Any conclusively observed primary gate failure returns KEEP_SYNC_BASELINE. Missing registered pairs, unknown required accounting or prerequisite blockage returns INCONCLUSIVE and does not publish a new supported profile.

D12 — Separate measurement, decision and publication. `run.mjs` produces append-only raw evidence; a deterministic `accept.mjs` reducer consumes the frozen cohort/threshold contract and emits a decision artifact; Jev independently evaluates the exact delivered candidate/evidence. Jev validates the delivery claims but does not rewrite the deterministic reducer outcome.

D13 — Add a narrow package-level `execution-profile.js` contract because the package ships only `src/` and currently exports no supported execution profile. It defines `CoreExecutionProfile.CORE_SYNC`, `CoreExecutionProfile.CORE_ASYNC_FIRST_V1`, the supported selection, evidence binding and `rollbackProfile: CORE_SYNC`. It does not silently alter `createAgentRuntime()` defaults; downstream BB-066 must consume the exported selection explicitly.

D14 — Profile selection is immutable for an active coordinator/session. Rollback from async to sync applies to new sessions after active async work is quiescent/reconciled; it must not reinterpret in-flight coordinator/effect state or duplicate external effects. CORE_SYNC remains an always-available compatibility profile.

D15 — The published profile binds exact decision artifact hash, heldout protocol hash, provider/model profile, BB-077–080 delivered artifact hashes and evaluated source SHA. Any later source/profile mutation makes that evidence binding stale and requires a new acceptance cohort/version before claiming the changed async profile remains evidence-backed.

D16 — If the reducer returns KEEP_SYNC_BASELINE, BB-081 can still be delivered successfully: the supported profile remains CORE_SYNC, async modules remain available only as non-default/experimental capability, and the evidence/limitations are published. If the reducer returns INCONCLUSIVE, BB-081 is not acceptance-complete and no supported-profile change is published.

D17 — External evidence is methodology/context only. OpenAI eval guidance supports repeatable task-specific datasets, full logging and pass/fail/pairwise grading for variable generative systems; SWE-bench requires isolated reproducible evaluation and warns against multi-attempt pass@k-style result selection. Unreal Agent's benchmark remains external evidence until reproduced by this exact ExHarness cohort.

expectedDependencyOutputs: BB-077 DONE: frozen benchmark registry/provider/accounting contract plus synchronous control evidence.
BB-078 DONE: detached-operation scheduling/recovery/cancel implementation and judgment.
BB-079 DONE: append-only async-result/provider compatibility implementation and judgment.

implementationSlices: S1 — At worker start resolve exact DONE BB-077/078/079/080 implementation-result, judgment and Living refs. Materialize a dependency manifest with exact hashes/profile identities. Any missing/incompatible delivered contract stops as PLAN_INPUT_CONTRADICTION before HOLD-* exposure.

S2 — Materialize and hash the held-out contract from BB-077: exactly HOLD-F01/F02/C01/C02, hidden expected-output digests, fixed provider/model, budgets, frozen prices, primary gates, deterministic arm order and fresh-reset/session rules. Refuse DEV-* or unregistered task execution in heldout mode.

S3 — Extend the existing benchmark runner/report path with `--mode heldout` and exact SYNC/ASYNC arm binding. Persist append-only request/attempt/task evidence for both arms; count failures/retries/unknown usage and prevent cross-arm workspace/session/cache-state leakage.

S4 — Add deterministic independent acceptance for task result/call/effect conditions and `accept.mjs` for the frozen three-way decision. Tests cover every gate independently, missing accounting, missing pair, safety regression, quality regression, success-only filtering attempts and a fully passing synthetic cohort.

S5 — Execute the full live four-pair held-out cohort using the exact credential-bearing BB-077 provider profile. No task replacement or manual rescue. If credentials/provider prerequisites are absent, emit PREREQUISITE_BLOCKED/INCONCLUSIVE and do not publish a supported-profile change.

S6 — Produce raw evidence plus paired report: accepted outcomes, all attempts, prompt/output/cached/cache-write tokens, provider/normalized cost, model turns, tool/capability calls, useful operations/turn, overlap, elapsed time, steering latency, recovery results and duplicate-effect count. Preserve unknown fields as null+reason.

S7 — Compute the deterministic decision. PROMOTE_ASYNC only when every BB-077 quality/safety/efficiency gate passes; any conclusive gate failure yields KEEP_SYNC_BASELINE; incomplete/unknown required evidence yields INCONCLUSIVE.

S8 — Add/export `execution-profile.js` with both CORE_SYNC and CORE_ASYNC_FIRST_V1 descriptors, evidence binding, supported selection and rollbackProfile CORE_SYNC. For KEEP_SYNC the selection remains sync. For PROMOTE_ASYNC select async explicitly. Never alter active-session state or implicit AgentRuntime defaults.

S9 — Update Core Living Docs with the supported profile, exact evidence scope, provider compatibility, rollback/quiescence rule and limitations. Run full Core regression plus profile tests and submit exact candidate/evidence to independent Jev delivery evaluation.

negativeVerificationCases: A DEV-* task, replacement task or newly authored task enters the held-out denominator after candidate work exists.
One arm reuses the other arm's workspace, provider session_id, runtime events or fixture state.
A failed/rate-limited/retried attempt is omitted from token/cost/elapsed totals or denominator.
A second successful attempt is selected best-of-k while the first failed attempt is hidden.
Missing cached/input/cost usage is converted to zero or inferred from stable-prefix bytes.
PROMOTE_ASYNC is emitted when accepted-task rate regresses or any primary BB-077 efficiency threshold fails.
PROMOTE_ASYNC is emitted with duplicate effects, unsafe cancellation, lost terminal result, stale-model dispatch or unresolved effect ambiguity.
INCONCLUSIVE evidence publishes CORE_ASYNC_FIRST_V1 as supported.
Jev prose or worker-authored summary overrides the deterministic reducer decision.
Supported profile changes to async while one dependency is not DONE or its delivered artifact hash differs.
Rollback changes the profile of an active async session before pending operations/effects are quiescent/reconciled.
A later source/profile mutation retains the old evidence binding and still claims the changed async profile is evidence-backed.

exact READY plan + DONE direct dependencies

livingDocs.statement: BB-081 Living Docs describe only the implemented and independently verified async-efficiency behavior, fallback and recovery limitations.

heldoutContract.attempts: Use BB-077 maxAttemptsPerTask=2 as bounded failure/retry ceiling. Every attempt is recorded; no best-of-k or task replacement.
heldoutContract.isolation: Fresh workspace/runtime/executor/event state and unique provider session_id per arm/task execution.
heldoutContract.statistics: Complete paired cohort product gate. Pair-level values and medians are primary; bootstrap intervals are descriptive only and no significance claim is made.

decisionContract.quality: candidate acceptedTaskRate >= CORE_SYNC on complete registered cohort
decisionContract.safety: duplicateEffects == 0 and all required recovery/cancel/stale-model/lost-result negatives pass
decisionContract.promote: Complete matched cohort AND quality pass AND safety pass AND every efficiency gate pass.
decisionContract.keepSync: Complete/known cohort with any conclusively failed quality, safety or primary efficiency gate.
decisionContract.inconclusive: Missing pair, incomplete heldout execution, unknown required accounting, prerequisite blockage or invalidated protocol binding.
decisionContract.authority: Deterministic reducer decision; independent Jev validates exact delivery evidence but cannot rewrite reducer outcome.

profiles.CORE_ASYNC_FIRST_V1: Selectable supported profile only after PROMOTE_ASYNC.

profilePublicationContract.selection: PROMOTE_ASYNC => CORE_ASYNC_FIRST_V1; KEEP_SYNC_BASELINE => CORE_SYNC; INCONCLUSIVE => no publication/change.
profilePublicationContract.noImplicitDefault: createAgentRuntime behavior is not silently changed by BB-081; consumers such as BB-066 resolve the exported supported profile explicitly.
profilePublicationContract.rollbackBoundary: New/quiescent session after all in-flight async operations/effects are terminal or reconciled.

researchEvidence.finding: Canonical READY research pre-registers HOLD-F01/F02/C01/C02, exact OpenRouter/Claude Sonnet 4.6 provider profile, fresh-reset rules, maxAttemptsPerTask=2, accounting semantics and the primary quality/safety/efficiency gates that BB-081 must not tune post hoc.

Phase contract explicitly reserves BB-081 for PROMOTE_ASYNC or KEEP_SYNC_BASELINE from held-out matched evidence and requires failures/retries, quality, cost/token, turns, overlap, recovery and duplicate-effect reporting.
The package publishes only `src`, so a supported profile intended for downstream BB-066 consumption must live behind a source/export contract rather than an unshipped benchmark-only file.
Current public exports contain AgentRuntime/model/effect surfaces but no supported execution-profile selection seam.
EffectOperation replay/reconciliation remains the semantic authority that held-out safety probes must preserve; benchmark/profile state cannot substitute for it.

Current evaluation guidance emphasizes task-specific repeatable datasets, logging all outcomes and reliable pass/fail or pairwise grading for variable generative systems; this supports a frozen cohort and independent exact acceptance rather than vibe-based selection.
SWE-bench uses isolated reproducible task evaluation with per-instance reports and run identity; result caches require distinct run identities when predictions differ.
